blocks.html: Greetings and Salutations!

items.html: Paul, and Silvanus, and Timothy, unto the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:
Grace unto you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We are bound to thank God always for you, brethren, as it is meet, because that your faith groweth exceedingly, and the charity of every one of you all toward each other aboundeth;
So that we ourselves glory in you in the churches of God for your patience and faith in all your persecutions and tribulations that ye endure:
Which is a manifest token of the righteous judgment of God, that ye may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which ye also suffer:

blocks.html:
Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy [1]

to the church in Thessalonica.

Jesus will come in flaming fire

(to take vengeance on nonbelievers)

items.html: Seeing it is a righteous thing with God to recompense tribulation to them that trouble you;

blocks.html: It is a righteous thing for God to punish those who trouble you.

items.html: And to you who are troubled rest with us, when the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels,

blocks.html: Jesus and his mighty angels

items.html: In flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not God, and that obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ:

blocks.html:
will come in flaming fire to take vengeance

on those who don't know God and disobey the gospel.

items.html: Who shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his power;

blocks.html: They will be punished with everlasting destruction,

items.html: When he shall come to be glorified in his saints, and to be admired in all them that believe (because our testimony among you was believed) in that day.
Wherefore also we pray always for you, that our God would count you worthy of this calling, and fulfil all the good pleasure of his goodness, and the work of faith with power:
That the name of our Lord Jesus Christ may be glorified in you, and ye in him, according to the grace of our God and the Lord Jesus Christ.

blocks.html:
when he comes to be glorified by his saints

and admired by all who believe (because of our preaching).

footnotes.html:
Paul ... unto the church of the Thessalonians. (v.1)

Although this epistle claims to have been written by Paul, many scholars think it was a forgery.

Bart D. Ehrman, The New Testament: A Historical Introlduction to the Early Christian Writings, 3rd ed. (2004), chap.23

blocks.html: Don't be fooled - Jesus isn't coming soon

items.html: Now we beseech you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him,
That ye be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand.

blocks.html: Don't be fooled by those who claim to have received a letter from us saying that Jesus has already returned. [1]

items.html: Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition;

blocks.html:
Don't let anyone deceive you.

That day won't come until many stop believing,

and a man of sin, the son of perdition, is revealed,

items.html: Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped; so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God.

blocks.html:
who will exalt himself above God,

and will be worshiped as God in the temple.

items.html: Remember ye not, that, when I was yet with you, I told you these things?

blocks.html: Don't you remember that I told you these things? [2]

items.html: And now ye know what withholdeth that he might be revealed in his time.
For the mystery of iniquity doth already work: only he who now letteth will let, until he be taken out of the way.

blocks.html:
Now you know that he'll be revealed in his time.

His iniquity is already at work,

but someone is holding him back.

And he won't be revealed until

that person is taken out of the way.

items.html: And then shall that Wicked be revealed, whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming:

blocks.html:
When the wicked one appears,

the Lord will kill him by breathing on him.

items.html: Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders,
And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish; because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved.

blocks.html:
He will come after the all-powerful Satan appears [3]

with all his signs and wonders.

God will send then strong delusion

(so they believe a lie and be damned)

items.html: And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie:

blocks.html:
God will send them strong delusion,

that they believe a lie,

items.html: That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.

blocks.html: so that they all will be damned. [4]

items.html: But we are bound to give thanks always to God for you, brethren beloved of the Lord, because God hath from the beginning chosen you to salvation through sanctification of the Spirit and belief of the truth:

blocks.html:
But we thank God for you,

because God chose you for salvation from the beginning. [5]

items.html: Whereunto he called you by our gospel, to the obtaining of the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.

blocks.html:
He called you to believe our gospel,

and thereby obtain the glory of Jesus.

items.html: Therefore, brethren, stand fast, and hold the traditions which ye have been taught, whether by word, or our epistle.

blocks.html:
So hold on to the traditions that you've been taught,

by word, or from our letter.

items.html: Now our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God, even our Father, which hath loved us, and hath given us everlasting consolation and good hope through grace,
Comfort your hearts, and stablish you in every good word and work.

footnotes.html:
Be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand. (v.2)

The author, who claims to be Paul (but probably wasn't), contradicts what the real Paul said in 1 Thessalonians (4:13-17) -- that Jesus would be returning soon, within Paul's lifetime.

This "Paul" says to ignore another letter that he supposedly wrote.

What letter is being referred to here? Is it 1 Thessalonians? If so, then should Christians not read it to avoid being "shaken in mind?"

If Paul wrote this letter (and many scholars think he didn't), then he is changing his mind since writing 1 Thessalonians about the timing of the Christ's return. The day of the Lord is no longer at hand. In fact it's nowhere near. Many things must happen first: there will be a great "falling away", a "man of sin" will be revealed, and Satan will show off his power by doing all kinds of signs and wonders.

Is the Day of the Lord at hand?

See Bart D. Ehrman, The New Testament: A Historical Introlduction to the Early Christian Writings, 3rd ed. (2004), chap.23

Remember ye not, that, when I was yet with you, I told you these things? (v.5)

No, they don't remember. Because the real Paul told them exactly the opposite in 1 Thessalonians.

Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders. (v.9)

Satan, not God, is all-powerful.

Can only God work wonders?

God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: That they all might be damned. (vv.11-12)

God will cause us to believe lies so that he can damn us to hell.

Do humans have free will?

Does God lie?

Does God want some people to go to hell?

Who forces non-believers to disbelieve?

[embedded video]

God hath from the beginning chosen you to salvation. (v.13)

God selects those who are to be saved (or damned) "from the beginning." It therefore makes no difference how good, kind, honest, or loving we may be; if God hasn't chosen us, we will be damned.

blocks.html: Pray for us

items.html: Finally, brethren, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may have free course, and be glorified, even as it is with you:
And that we may be delivered from unreasonable and wicked men: for all men have not faith.
But the Lord is faithful, who shall stablish you, and keep you from evil.
And we have confidence in the Lord touching you, that ye both do and will do the things which we command you.
And the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God, and into the patient waiting for Christ.

blocks.html: Pray for us.
Whoever doesn't work, shouldn't eat

items.html: Now we command you, brethren, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that ye withdraw yourselves from every brother that walketh disorderly, and not after the tradition which he received of us.

blocks.html:
We command you to shun those who don't accept the teaching

that you've received from us. [1]

items.html: For yourselves know how ye ought to follow us: for we behaved not ourselves disorderly among you;

blocks.html: Because you know how well behaved we were with you.

items.html: Neither did we eat any man's bread for nought; but wrought with labour and travail night and day, that we might not be chargeable to any of you:

blocks.html:
We worked night and day,

so you wouldn't have to provide for us.

items.html: Not because we have not power, but to make ourselves an example unto you to follow us.

blocks.html: We did this to set an example for you.

items.html: For even when we were with you, this we commanded you, that if any would not work, neither should he eat.

blocks.html:
When we were with you we commanded you,

that whoever refused to work, should not eat. [2]

items.html: For we hear that there are some which walk among you disorderly, working not at all, but are busybodies.

blocks.html:
We hear that there are some lazy people among you

who don't work, but are busybodies.

items.html: Now them that are such we command and exhort by our Lord Jesus Christ, that with quietness they work, and eat their own bread.
But ye, brethren, be not weary in well doing.

blocks.html: We command them to work to pay for their own food.
Shun those who refuse to obey us

items.html: And if any man obey not our word by this epistle, note that man, and have no company with him, that he may be ashamed.
Yet count him not as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother.

blocks.html:
If any refuse to obey our words in this letter,

note who they are,

and shun them so they will be ashamed.
I, Paul, am writing this with my own hand

items.html: Now the Lord of peace himself give you peace always by all means. The Lord be with you all.

blocks.html: May the Lord of peace give you peace. [3]

items.html: The salutation of Paul with mine own hand, which is the token in every epistle: so I write.

blocks.html:
I, Paul, am signing this letter with my own hand,

as I do with every letter that I write. [4]

items.html: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

blocks.html: Amen.

footnotes.html:
Withdraw yourselves from every brother that walketh disorderly, and not after the tradition which he received of us. (v.6)

If any man obey not our word by this epistle, note that man, and have no company with him. (v.14)

Jehovah's Witnesses use these verses to justify disfellowshipping anyone who disagrees with the Watchtower's teachings.

If any would not work, neither should he eat. (v.10)

Those who will not or cannot work should starve to death.

Rep. Stephen Fincher (R-TN) quoted this verse to justify his vote against funding for SNAP (the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, formerly known as food stamps).

The Lord of peace. (v.16)

Is God warlike or peaceful?

The salutation of Paul with mine own hand, which is the token in every epistle: so I write. (v.17)

The author claims to be Paul, and offers proof by saying that he's ending his letter and signing it in the same way as he always does. But the real Paul didn't end most of his other (undisputed) letters in this way, including 1 Thessalonians.
